scope.flow: Nested multicall() batches executed via delegatecall with a post-batch ETH balance equality check
scope.environment: Covenant contract with MulticallLib.multicall() delegatecall batching

statements.text: An outer multicall() batch is executed with a nonzero top-level msg.value that the outer batch intends to forward later.
An inner multicall() is nested within the outer batch and executes via delegatecall in the same execution context.
The inner multicall() does not itself forward any ETH.

Each nesting level computes balanceBeforeCall using the same top-level msg.value because inner batches execute via delegatecall, and there is no notion of per-batch consumed value, so the inner multicall() assumes the entire transaction msg.value must be fully balanced within its own sub-batch.

The inner batch computes balanceBeforeCall = (prevBalance + msg.value) - msg.value = prevBalance while the actual end-of-inner-batch balance remains prevBalance + msg.value, so the equality check fails.

The post-batch ETH balance equality check should be enforced only at the outermost multicall level, so nested batches are not required to balance the entire transaction msg.value within their own sub-batch.

Nested multicalls should remain composable and not revert in benign cases such as an inner batch that does nothing, so integrations relying on multi-level batching and deferred ETH forwarding within the outer batch continue to work.

ambiguities: No explicit caller/authorization condition is stated for invoking multicall(); the report does not say anyone can call it.
The report describes the nested-batch revert as a conditional scenario (if/when nested with msg.value), not an observed transaction; no concrete prior transaction state is supplied.
The exact balanceBeforeCall/end-balance values are given only as the inner batch's own computation, so they are treated as root-cause mechanism rather than preconditions.
